title: Access Certification & Licensing Evidence - Ops Sync
summary: Working sync to align on access certification runbook, gather evidence for upcoming internal audit, finalise licensing invoices mapping and confirm service account decommission timeline. Agreed next steps around evidence bundle, Okta export, and scheduled access recertification window.
topics: backup and retention window for legal holds
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-25 16:00 UTC | Duration 47m | Attendees listed above

[00:00] Jordan Patel: All right good afternoon, everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, objective today is to lock down what goes into the audit evidence bundle and confirm owners for access certification.

[00:22] Speaker 2 (Amina?): Yep, hi all, Amina here, sorry I'm on a slightly delayed connection so if I drop a beat that's why.

[00:35] Eli Carter: Legal on the line, hey, we have the SOC2 request coming in and they want explicit access lists and manifest of privileged keys, and we need that by the 8th. Is that correct Jordan?

[00:52] Jordan Patel: That's what I saw, yeah 2026-12-08 is the internal audit window. We need an evidence pack a few days prior, so target for pack is the 4th.

[01:10] Sam O'Leary: Quick clarity, when you say privileged keys do you mean user-facing SSO sessions or GCP service account keys and any HSM/KMS usage?

[01:25] Amina Singh: Both, ideally. The ask explicitly calls out service account keys, KMS key usage logs, and privileged role assignments in Okta and GCP. There's some overlap with billing artifacts that Tessa might have.

[01:40] Tessa Liu: Yup, I can pull licensing invoices mapped by seat and by vendor, I have the spend reports but I need to reconcile them with the contracts.

[01:51] [00:02:00] Marco Reyes: We should also include a snapshot of RBAC from the console and a CSV export from Okta with groups, user-to-group mapping and last auth timestamp. I can run those exports but need an approved runtime so we don't overload the directory services.

[02:20] Dana Brooks: Procurement — we need the vendor license tiers for the last 12 months to show compliance with entitlements, some of the auditors like to see purchase order numbers tied to invoices.

[02:38] Jordan Patel: OK, plan suggestion: Marco runs the Okta and GCP IAM exports by Nov 30, Amina will produce the KMS/rotation logs, Tessa will reconcile invoices and attach POs, Eli & Priya will validate legal formatting. We'll capture action items in a shared doc.

[03:05] [00:03:30] Priya Nair: One nuance — our retention policy for logs is 90 days by default in the cheap tier. The audit may ask for 12 months. Do we have a cold store for older KMS audit logs?

[03:22] Sam O'Leary: We do keep an archive bucket in GCS with 1yr retention for audit logs but the ingestion varies; the problem is some service account rotation logs were not forwarded to archive for a period in May.

[03:40] Amina Singh: Right that's the gap I flagged in the risk register. We need to surface any missing windows in the evidence pack and provide mitigations.

[03:53] [00:04:15] Jordan Patel: Good. Practical questions: what format does legal want? PDF single bundle, or a folder of CSVs and exported logs?

[04:06] Eli Carter: Prefer a bundled zip with a manifest CSV that lists each file, owner, and date range; put a short readme explaining any gaps. PDF or docs are fine for narrative sections.

[04:22] [00:04:45] Speaker 3 (Sam?): Reason — manifest makes it much easier for the SOC reviewer to trawl.

[04:32] Tessa Liu: I'll prepare the invoice reconciliation sheet and include a column for PO and contract link. I'll also flag items where we need procurement to backfill missing POs.

[04:45] Dana Brooks: I'll run a PO lookup and fill in missing numbers by Dec 2.

[04:56] [00:05:20] Jordan Patel: On access certification: do we run a system-driven recertification or rely on manager attestations? Our identity provider supports automated recert flows but it needs manager approvals.

[05:14] Amina Singh: For privileged roles we want manager attestation plus automated removal of stale accounts older than 90 days. For normal roles automated recert is fine. We need to document the threshold rules.

[05:27] Priya Nair: Can we capture the last login time and inactivity window in the manifest so auditors see that inactive accounts were removed?

[05:36] Marco Reyes: Yes I'll include last auth timestamp from Okta export and a script output showing which accounts were disabled as part of the 90-day policy.

[05:50] [00:06:10] Speaker 2: Note, sometimes Okta exports muddy the group names, I often see Ockta spelled wrong in downstream scripts, just a heads up that the CSV may have odd columns.

[06:03] Jordan Patel: Good catch — we'll sanity check column headers.

[06:14] [00:06:35] Sam O'Leary: Another risk is service accounts used by older CI jobs — we have about 17 service accounts that are unowned in the inventory. Need to assign owners or schedule decomm.

[06:29] Amina Singh: We put a temporary hold on decomm until we confirm which ones are used in prod. Could we do a quick run to detect active keys and last-used timestamps?

[06:41] Marco Reyes: I can run a last-used report against service account keys and produce a 'suspect' list. That will take a day to validate with CI owners.

[06:53] [00:07:10] Jordan Patel: Timing — can we aim to have the suspect list and initial owners by Dec 1 so decomm windows can begin Dec 6?

[07:03] Marco Reyes: Yes Dec 1 for the suspect list, and we propose a decomm window that is 2 weeks long so owners can raise issues.

[07:17] Tessa Liu: Also note that decomm impacts billing for some vendors where seat counts change when service accounts are removed — I'll map any potential licensing impact.

[07:28] [00:07:45] Priya Nair: For legal holds, if there's any ongoing e-discovery, we need to snapshot relevant buckets before decomm. Are we aware of any active holds?

[07:39] Eli Carter: Not currently, but I'll double-check and flag any matters by Nov 28.

[07:46] [00:08:10] Jordan Patel: Great — now a practical checklist for the evidence pack: Okta CSV, GCP IAM CSV, KMS access logs, service account last-used report, invoice reconciliation, PO mapping, readme, manifest. Anything missing?

[08:02] Dana Brooks: Add the policy doc showing our 90-day inactivity rule and the last update timestamp of that policy.

[08:12] Amina Singh: And include the RBAC role definitions export from the console. Sometimes the role text gets truncated when exported, so include a screenshot for critical roles.

[08:25] [00:08:40] Speaker 3 (Sam): Screenshots are helpful, yes.

[08:32] Jordan Patel: Ok we'll do both CSV and screenshot for the top 10 privileged roles.

[08:40] [00:09:00] Tessa Liu: Question on storage — where do we put the final zip? S3 or internal share? It contains sensitive PII in logs, right?

[08:52] Priya Nair: Use the encrypted internal evidence bucket with restricted ACLs. We have a retention rule to delete after the audit plus 30 days. Ensure the bucket encryption keys are rotated and note that in the manifest.

[09:07] Marco Reyes: That bucket is in project infra-audit, I have write access, I'll create a folder named 2026-12-evidence and set a lifecycle.

[09:15] [00:09:40] Jordan Patel: We need to list who will have access to the evidence bundle. The auditors will get temporary read-only access and Legal gets full access.

[09:26] Eli Carter: Correct. Provide a time-limited signed URL for the auditors and put an access log in the manifest.

[09:36] [00:10:00] Marco Reyes: Ok, I'll enable object level logging for the folder and include the access log export in the bundle.

[09:44] [00:10:20] Speaker 2: Quick note — check the format of KMS logs, they're nested JSONs and sometimes our download script flattens them poorly. We'll need to keep raw logs as well as a parsed CSV.

[09:57] Amina Singh: I'm on it, I'll produce both raw JSON slices and a parsed view with the important fields: principal, key_id, operation, timestamp.

[10:10] [00:10:45] Dana Brooks: Procurement question — Tessa will you need PO numbers back to 2019? The auditors asked for 'historical entitlements' sometimes they go back several years.

[10:22] Tessa Liu: I can pull vendors back to 2019 but it will take longer to validate. For now we'll prioritize the last 24 months and surface older items if requested.

[10:35] Jordan Patel: Good pragmatic approach.

[10:41] [00:11:05] Priya Nair: On the certification flow, who will run manager attestations? Do managers get an automated email from Okta or do we do a manual spreadsheet?

[10:54] Marco Reyes: Okta has Certify flows we can trigger; they send emails and require manager responses. I need to coordinate with HR for reporting managers mapping.

[11:06] Amina Singh: Let's do automated for non-privileged, manual for privileged roles as we said earlier. We'll record manager attestations in the manifest with attestation timestamp.

[11:18] [00:11:40] Jordan Patel: There's a small friction: managers sometimes ignore the emails. What's our escalation path when attestations are overdue?

[11:29] Eli Carter: Legal suggests we have a secondary approver or flag to security for intervention after 7 days overdue; document that in the policy.

[11:43] [00:12:00] Tessa Liu: I can run a weekly report of open attestations and send a summary to managers with a cc to their director.

[11:52] Sam O'Leary: Also consider adding a Slack reminder integration for managers, that tends to increase response rates.

[12:00] Jordan Patel: Great, Marco can look at Okta's webhook for Slack pings.

[12:09] [00:12:25] Amina Singh: Another topic: evidence of key rotations. We need to show rotation events and who approved them for KMS and any HSMs.

[12:21] Marco Reyes: I can pull rotation events but approvals are in the ticketing system — we'll need cross-reference to ticket IDs. The ticket export will be included.

[12:34] [00:12:55] Speaker 3: Note, sometimes ticket IDs are missing in rotation scripts, we should standardize a tag.

[12:42] Jordan Patel: Action item: require that any key rotation includes a ticket reference in the commit message. We'll roll that out as a policy change.

[12:51] [00:13:10] Priya Nair: For the short term, include partial evidence and a remediation plan that explains where the ticket references are missing and how we'll prevent recurrence.

[13:03] [00:13:30] Tessa Liu: Switching to licensing — I noticed a couple of vendor line items with ambiguous cost centers, we need procurement help to allocate. This affects our unit economics reporting.

[13:15] Dana Brooks: I will map the cost centers and get back with a mapping doc by Dec 2.

[13:26] [00:13:55] Jordan Patel: Good. Ok, let's go through explicit owners and due dates now.

[13:34] Amina Singh: Owner: Amina — KMS logs extraction and parsed CSV — due Nov 30.

[13:42] Marco Reyes: Owner: Marco — Okta/GCP IAM exports, last-used report for service accounts, access logs for evidence bucket — due Nov 30.

[13:52] Tessa Liu: Owner: Tessa — invoice reconciliation and PO mapping (24 months priority) — due Dec 2.

[14:00] Eli Carter: Owner: Eli & Priya — legal formatting and readme, check for e-discovery holds — due Nov 28.

[14:09] Dana Brooks: Owner: Dana — PO lookup and procurement mapping — due Dec 2.

[14:17] Jordan Patel: I'll collate everything and produce the manifest and the zip packaging steps — I'll aim to have a draft manifest Dec 1.

[14:27] [00:14:55] Speaker 2: A couple of practical caveats: exports sometimes truncate usernames with unicode; watch for encoding issues when you open CSVs in Excel.

[14:40] Marco Reyes: Noted, will export as UTF-8 and include a readme about how to open files.

[14:50] [00:15:15] Jordan Patel: Any blockers?

[14:54] Priya Nair: The only blocker is the archival gap in May — we need to state that explicitly and show investigation notes.

[15:02] Amina Singh: Also need HR to confirm manager mappings for a small subset of contractors. I'll open a ticket.

[15:12] Dana Brooks: Procurement has one vendor piece where the PO is missing; I'm on it.

[15:20] [00:15:50] Jordan Patel: OK, let's recap next steps.

[15:24] Jordan Patel: Recap: Marco and Amina exports by Nov 30, Tessa and Dana invoice/PO mapping by Dec 2, Eli/Priya legal checks by Nov 28, Jordan will draft manifest by Dec 1. We'll sync again Dec 3 for readiness review.

[15:40] [00:16:20] Jordan Patel: Any final concerns?

[15:44] Sam O'Leary: Might be useful to have a quick dry-run of the zip and access logging to ensure the auditors can open things. Could schedule a 20-minute test with a friendly auditor.

[15:55] Eli Carter: We'll do the dry-run; I'll coordinate with a third-party reviewer and schedule tentatively for Dec 6.

[16:03] [00:16:45] Jordan Patel: Perfect. Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourn.

[16:10] End of transcript. Some timestamps approximate, transcription contains slight name transcription errors (e.g., Ockta for Okta).
next_steps: Marco: run Okta and GCP IAM exports and service account last-used report by 2026-11-30
Amina: extract KMS rotation logs and produce parsed CSV by 2026-11-30
Tessa: reconcile invoices and map POs for last 24 months by 2026-12-02
Eli/Priya: validate legal formatting and confirm e-discovery holds by 2026-11-28
Jordan: produce draft manifest and packaging steps by 2026-12-01
Dana: procurement PO lookup and cost center mapping by 2026-12-02
Schedule dry-run with external reviewer on 2026-12-06 (Eli to coordinate)
action_items: Marco - Okta export, GCP IAM export, service account last-used report (due 2026-11-30)
Eli & Priya - Legal formatting, e-discovery check (due 2026-11-28)
Dana - PO lookup and procurement mapping (due 2026-12-02)
